A software startup proposal for advisers who want to give hands-on clients more control and reduce the work around each decision.

Explore the adviser workspace ↗

What your team gets.

  • A consolidated view of each client’s holdings, loans, liquidity and objectives.
  • A queue of investment requests with source records, assumptions, tax comparisons and open questions attached.
  • Contact details and previous interactions beside the review.
  • AI-assisted document intake, with extracted fields awaiting professional checks.
  • Versioned client instructions, signed authorisation and dependent execution steps.
  • Dated filing checklists, pre-filled figures and explicit questions.

All of these are demonstrated with fictional data. AI, providers and filings are not connected.

What the firm controls.

Review every recommendation and tax adjustment before showing it to the client. Approve or reject the route. Onboard your own clients. Decide which portfolios, providers and service scope you support.

A client can explore scenarios and request a review. A scenario is not released professional advice. Material changes to an approved plan require a fresh review and signature. Execution must verify funding, account permissions, limits and confirmed provider results.

Who could operate it?

A firm with wealth advice and tax accountancy in-house and appropriate FCA permissions and qualified tax accountancy, AML supervision and professional registrations. Legal work needs qualified lawyers where required. Registrations and permissions must be checked for the actual services and clients.

Being a software proposal does not remove advice, tax-agent, client-money, privacy or execution obligations. Operating arrangements would need professional design before launch.

Validate the economics.

The working price is £10,000 annually per client office, with professional fees separate. This needs testing against client value, staff time, provider costs and support requirements.

Use a small cohort to measure document handling, time per review, filing corrections, completion rates and the client experience. No proven efficiency gain or revenue uplift is claimed.

The questions to answer.

  1. Which existing clients would ask for this?
  2. What would make it worth the proposed price?
  3. Which providers and accounting systems must connect first?
  4. Which steps would the firm trust the system to prepare or execute?
  5. Would your firm want to build and operate it?
